[Section] Experiments
[source_id=44] We apply our adaptively sparse Transformers on four machine translation tasks. For comparison, a natural baseline is the standard Transformer architecture using the softmax transform in its multi-head attention mechanisms. We consider two other model variants in our experiments that make use of different normalizing transformations:
[source_id=45] 1.5-entmax: a Transformer with sparse entmax attention with fixed $\alpha =1.5$ for all heads. This is a novel model, since 1.5-entmax had only been proposed for RNN-based NMT models BIBREF14, but never in Transformers, where attention modules are not just one single component of the seq2seq model but rather an integral part of all of the model components.
[source_id=46] $\alpha $-entmax: an adaptive Transformer with sparse entmax attention with a different, learned $\alpha _{i,j}^t$ for each head.
[source_id=47] The adaptive model has an additional scalar parameter per attention head per layer for each of the three attention mechanisms (encoder self-attention, context attention, and decoder self-attention), i.e.,
[source_id=48] and we set $\alpha _{i,j}^t = 1 + \operatornamewithlimits{\mathsf {sigmoid}}(a_{i,j}^t) \in ]1, 2[$. All or some of the $\alpha $ values can be tied if desired, but we keep them independent for analysis purposes.
